newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - March 19.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - March 19.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sri Lankan press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
Four Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) suicide bombers in Colombo to allegedly assassinate unidentified VIP, police say.
All liquor outlets closed for three days from Thursday in bid to hold trouble-free election on Friday.

LTTE guerrillas plotting to assassinate Prime Minister Sirima Bandaranaike and her son Anura Bandaranaike, who is a member of the main opposition United National Party (UNP), according to officials of the police criminal investigations department.
Government likely to impose curfew soon after polling ends in Friday's election, defence sources say.
Unknown people grab 800 polling cards from remote post office in the northwest. Police warn of severe punishment for those found stuffing ballot boxes at Friday's election.
Ownership of more than 15,000 acres of farmland to be given to farmers who work them now, government says.
